newsitem.title: USA: Amoco says sets plans on $18-$21/barrel oil.
newsitem.headline: Amoco says sets plans on $18-$21/barrel oil.

text.p: Amoco Corp said its operational strategies are based on the mid- to long-term assumption that oil prices will be the $18 to $21 per barrel range.
"Our planning going forward is based on prices of oil in the $18 to $21 range, rather than what we have today, which is much higher than that," said Amoco chairman Laurance Fuller.
January oil futures traded Tuesday above $25 per barrel, while the October contract was just above $20 per barrel.

Referring to sales of oil by Iraq and their impact on the oil market, Fuller said in a conference call, "It appears to me that the Iraqi sale has been dwarfed by other events in the short-term marketplace, which is to say that cold weather and relatively high world demand have caused the price of oil briefly to go up very substantially."
He added, "I do not personally believe in the medium to long-term that we can expect substantially higher oil prices because I think that there's plenty of oil in the world."
Fuller also said Amoco's proposed capital and exploration spending budget for 1997 of $4.1 billion includes additional spending on its convenience stores and its joint ventures with McDonald's Corp.
"We expect to put more new service stations on-stream next year than we did this year," Fuller said.
"On the refining side, which is the most depressed part of our business and has been during 1996, we have plans in place to continue to reduce our costs and increase yields," he said.

"Between cost reduction and yield improvement, we would expect, and have budgeted, an increase in profitability and therefore a reduction in cost in the range of $100 million a year before tax. We expect to improve beyond next year in addition to that," Fuller said.
